recipes.name: Mom's Spaghetti Bolognese
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil. Stir in spaghetti and return to a boil. Cook spaghetti uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 12 minutes; drain.

Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add bacon. Cook, turning occasionally, until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Add onion, celery, carrot, and oregano to bacon; continue cooking until vegetables begin to soften, 8 to 10 minutes. Add garlic; cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Crumble in ground beef; cook and stir until no longer pink and completely cooked, 8 to 10 minutes.

Pour vinegar over ground beef mixture; simmer until liquid evaporates, about 5 minutes. Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, and sugar; bring to a boil, season with salt and black pepper, then remove from heat. Stir in basil .
Spoon sauce over spaghetti; top with Parmesan cheese to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Spaghetti Bolognese
raw_recipe.description: This version of a classic Italian dish combines bacon with ground beef and canned crushed tomatoes in a sauce to be served over spaghetti.

review.reviewBody: This was excellent!

I will NEVER EVER make another bolognese sauce again - this one was A-M-A-Z-I-N-G!! I added a pound of ground Italian sausage, aside the ground beef called for (we like it meaty). I cooked the sauce at a low heat for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally. I also used low sodium crushed tomatoes and the basil called for but I added another 2 tbsp fresh basil after the 1.5 hrs of simmering - the flavor was delicious.

I did change a couple of things in this dish.

1st Change: Chunky chopped the carrots and celery.

2nd Change: 6 cloves of garlic 

3rd Change: Tablespoon of Paprika 

4th Change: Italian Herbs instead of Oregano.

Results: Beautiful, lots of flavour and texture
Best to make Monday and serve Friday. Aging is the key.

Made a double batch with venison. Rave reviews all around. The prep for chopping the veggies was the longest task, so I did those the night before. Added a few shakes of Worstershire sauce after the salt and pepper. Fabulous.

The only change I did was to do Step 1 last (so I started with Step 2), and added a tsp of dried Italian seasoning when I added the oregano. Because I flip- flopped, I simmered the sauce on low for the duration of the pasta cook time to allow the flavors to better meld. This makes a lot of sauce!! But, I think that’s the point of Bolognese? Overall, we really liked this. Thanks Mom and stefychefy!!

Love this recipe so much! The only changes I make are adding a few bay leaves when the balsamic vinegar goes in, and also I simmer it for at least 15 minutes at the end! If it’s just brought to the boil then removed from heat there is a lot of liquid and the flavours haven’t bound together.

Excellent.. I used the opion of wine rather thn vinegar. And I slow cooked th finished sauce for 3-4 hours using beef broth(and a littl more dry red wine) to thin as needed. I tasted the sauce at the point the recipe was complete and i think the slow cooking further improved a good sauce. I think the beef broth made it heartier with more complex flavor.
Absolutely delicious, my children love this! I did add a splash of red wine and let it all simmer for about an hour.
This turned out amazing. Its a keeper. Just added 1/4 cup of cabernet and instead of white sugar I used brown sugar. Family loved it

This was an awesome dinner for my family. I made it a little differently though. We used whole wheat pene pasta instead of spaghetti and added 1/2 cup of red wine as well as the balsamic vinegar. Our choice of meat was ground Italian sausage which made the flavor profile deep and rich with comforting goodness. A must save recipe.
The recipe was a great base for me. I used fresh tomatoes & added Italian Sausage. Great flavors!!
We really enjoyed this recipe. First attempt at a bolognese sauce, turned out wonderfully. Followed the recipe except used wine instead of balsamccic vinegar.
Good flavor, but did not say to strain any of the fat from the bacon or GB. May try that next time to make it a little less rich.
rich flavor, easy to make
wonderful! i added heavy cream and used a tad more balsamic, only beef and no pork... but i enjoyed spinning off of this
This is certainly not a real Bolognese. But it is a really good meat sauce.

While I enjoyed this sauce, I just cannot move all the way to 5 stars. First, as written it makes a BIG pot of sauce. That's good! But for the amount of ingredients and volume I think it certainly needs more italian seasoning than just a couple of teaspoons of oregano. That's really my only beef. Also I used balsamic vinegar but next time will go the red wine route. Good recipe as is, but could really stand out with deeper italian herbs. Thanks!
Really good! Really good flavor with the balsamic and bacon. Only tip would be to drain the bacon fat to make it less greasy and oily.

Very good!! My kids wanted it for dinner the next night too. I didn't have bacon, but will try it next time.
I added a little baking soda after tasting to help reduce the acid.
